Whole-token 0-1 time

Source: R/landmarks.R
normalise_time_token.Rd

Puts each token on one 0-1 time axis that runs from its first f0 to its last f0, so contour shapes can be compared. Adds the column token_t01. No landmarks are needed.

Usage

normalise_time_token(df, time, token, f0 = "f0")

Arguments

df

Data frame with the time, token and f0 columns.

time

Name of the time column. Only the order and spacing of times within a token matter.

token

Name of the token-ID column.

f0

Name of the f0 column that says which rows have f0. Default "f0". For F0 Correction output, pass f0 = "f0_corrected": left at the default, the tracked f0 would decide, with a message.

Value

df with token_t01 added (or replaced). A missing column is an error.

Details

Rows have f0 as in normalise_time_landmarks(): in a column in Hz, 0 is no f0, and a column with negative markers such as -1 is not read as Hz, so set those to NA first. Rows without f0 between the first and last f0 keep their place by time. Rows before the first f0 or after the last get NA, not 0 or 1, and so does every row of a token with f0 at fewer than two times and every row with no token. So removing rows without f0 does not change the column. A lone f0 sample in the silence, cut off by a gap, does become the first or last f0. contour_duration() anchors its span on runs of at least min_run = 2 samples by default, so for such a token its token_f0_dur is shorter than the stretch token_t01 covers. The Start page's option for short edge runs, or drop_rows_without_f0(min_run = 3), removes such samples first.

For a word of several syllables, token_t01 is the whole word: the stretch without f0 between the syllables and the syllables' duration ratio are kept. So the syllable boundary falls at a different point in each token and blurs when tokens are averaged. <tier>_tseq from normalise_time_landmarks() puts the syllables in sequence instead, so the boundaries line up, and <tier>_tbound puts them in sequence with the gap kept, so the TextGrid boundaries line up. A word tier's <word>_t01 gives the same values as token_t01 when all of the token's f0 lies inside the word interval.

The model fits rescale a time column the same way (resolve_time_norm() with f0), so a fit on the time column equals a fit on token_t01, apart from two cases. Tokens with f0 at one time only: the fits keep those at 0.5, while token_t01 is NA on them. And rows with no token: the fits treat them as one token of their own, while token_t01 is NA on them.

Columns made by shinytone 1.0.0 ran from each token's first row to its last, rows without f0 included. Make them again with this function.

See also

normalise_time_landmarks() for each syllable on its own axis, or the syllables in sequence.

Examples

df <- data.frame(token = rep(c("a", "b"), c(6, 5)),
                 time  = c(0:5, 0:4) / 100,
                 f0    = c(NA, 210, 215, NA, 220, NA, 180, 185, 190, 195, NA))
normalise_time_token(df, "time", "token")
#>    token time  f0 token_t01
#> 1      a 0.00  NA        NA
#> 2      a 0.01 210 0.0000000
#> 3      a 0.02 215 0.3333333
#> 4      a 0.03  NA 0.6666667
#> 5      a 0.04 220 1.0000000
#> 6      a 0.05  NA        NA
#> 7      b 0.00 180 0.0000000
#> 8      b 0.01 185 0.3333333
#> 9      b 0.02 190 0.6666667
#> 10     b 0.03 195 1.0000000
#> 11     b 0.04  NA        NA
